name: hcapp_setEventMessagesRead
description: NOTE: The filename has '_obsolete' suffix but the SP name in the DB is hcapp_setEventMessagesRead (no suffix). This SP was the predecessor to hcapp_getEventBadgeCount. It has a stricter eventId null check (validates when @resetAllBadgeCounts=0). The key difference from hcapp_getEventBadgeCount: the resetAll path filters EventMessage by UserId, whereas getEventBadgeCount updates LastSequenceCount from max across all messages. In the resetBadgeCount path, it uses UserId (not PublicHasherId) to look up the message.

parameters.name: resetBadgeCount
parameters.description: When non-zero, MERGE to mark event as read. Default 0.

parameters.name: resetAllBadgeCounts
parameters.description: When non-zero, resets all badge counts. Default 0.

rowsets.name: StandardErrors
rowsets.description: Standard error format. errorType=2 for null userId or null publicEventId (when not resetting all). errorType=3 for auth failure.

columns.name: badgeCount
columns.description: @messageSequenceCount - embc.LastSequenceCount. NULL if no badge record.

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.EventMessageBadgeCounts SET LastSequenceCount — when @resetAllBadgeCounts != 0 (filters by UserId, not PublicHasherId)

codeSmells.issue: File marked _obsolete but SP name in DB has no such suffix
codeSmells.detail: The filename is hcapp_setEventMessagesRead_obsolete.sql but the CREATE PROCEDURE name is hcapp_setEventMessagesRead. If deployed, this creates a live SP named hcapp_setEventMessagesRead, not _obsolete. HC6 decision needed: keep or remove?

codeSmells.issue: resetAll path filters by UserId not PublicHasherId
codeSmells.detail: hcapp_getEventBadgeCount uses LastSequenceCount from max across all EventMessages. This SP filters EventMessage by UserId=@userId in the UPDATE. The two SPs have subtly different reset semantics.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Confirm whether this SP is still in production use before HC6 migration
